tier_reason: Peer-reviewed OSDI'18 paper. It states the 99.7% vs 70% result for meeting a 150ms P99 goal (abstract, Fig. 3) and compares against two production policies (OneRFpolicy, which is a single shared off-the-shelf memcached cache, and TAO++) plus emulated LAMA, Cliffhanger and FAIR. The testbed code is public in the repo and the CPU is given (Azure D16 v3, E5-2673v3), but no compiler or flags are stated, so it is not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Under backend load spikes on the OneRF-modeled testbed, RobinHood meets a 150ms P99 request-latency goal 99.7% of the time, whereas the next best policy meets it only 70% of the time. Sec. 5.2 names the next best policy as OneRFpolicy, a single shared memcached cache matching Microsoft OneRF's production setup: it violates the 150ms P99 SLO 30% of the time vs <0.3% for RobinHood.
corrections.baseline: OneRFpolicy: a single shared off-the-shelf memcached cache per application server, matching Microsoft OneRF's production configuration. Also compared: TAO++ (static per-backend allocation) and emulated LAMA++, Cliffhanger++ and FAIR++.
corrections.hardware: 50 Microsoft Azure D16 v3 VMs: 2.4 GHz Intel E5-2673v3 (8 cores), 64GB memory, 400GB SSD, 8Gbit/s network
corrections.workload: Testbed of 16 application servers and 34 backend servers across 50 Azure VMs. The servers host 20 backend services (KV store, MySQL cluster, matrix-multiply recommender) modeled on OneRF's 20 most-queried backends. Each application server has a local 32GB memcached. Traffic comes from OneRF production statistics, averaging ~200k queries/s (500k peak), with injected backend load and latency spikes. The metric is the fraction of time a 150ms P99 request-latency SLO is met.
corrections.caveats: The metric is SLO attainment (share of time meeting a 150ms P99), not a throughput or speed ratio. The next-best baseline is a caching policy (one shared memcached cache without partitioning), not a slower memcached. RobinHood repartitions off-the-shelf memcached, so it is a cache resource-allocation system, not a new eviction algorithm. The testbed is Go plus a Python controller, last touched in 2019. No compiler or flags are stated.

notes: All metadata matched gh (BSD-3-Clause, 95 stars, last commit 2019-07-08, not archived, not a fork). The main fix is that the 70% 'next best' policy is OneRFpolicy (single shared cache), not a static-partitioning policy. Static partitioning is TAO++.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed SOSP'23 paper. It states S3-FIFO in CacheLib reaches >6x the throughput of CacheLib's optimized LRU at 16 threads, with a larger gap vs 2Q and TinyLFU (Sec. 1, Sec. 5.3, Fig. 8). The prototype benchmark code is public (Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23 mybench/, CMake RelWithDebInfo), but the paper names only CloudLab c6420 nodes, not a CPU model or compiler, so it is not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: S3-FIFO achieves more than 6x higher throughput than the highly-optimized LRU in Meta's CacheLib with 16 threads, at both small and large cache sizes (synthetic Zipf trace). The throughput gap is larger still vs CacheLib's optimized 2Q and TinyLFU. Separately, in libCacheSim simulation over 6594 traces from 14 datasets, S3-FIFO has lower miss ratios than state-of-the-art algorithms and the lowest mean miss ratio on 10 of the 14 datasets.
corrections.baseline: LRU (Meta CacheLib's optimized LRU; also CacheLib's optimized 2Q and TinyLFU, plus Segcache)
corrections.workload: Throughput: an S3-FIFO prototype in Meta CacheLib replays only a synthetic Zipf (alpha=1.0) trace. The trace is 100*n million requests over n million 4KB objects (n = thread count), run at 1-16 threads with a large cache (LRU miss ratio 0.02) and a small one (0.21). Miss ratio: libCacheSim simulation over 6594 production traces from 14 datasets (MSR, FIU, CloudPhysics, CDN1/2, Tencent, Wikimedia, Alibaba, Twitter, Meta KV/CDN, ...).
corrections.hardware: CloudLab Clemson c6420 nodes for the prototype (the paper does not name the CPU model). Turbo boost off, one thread pinned per core, all memory allocated on the same NUMA node with numactl.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Artifact build script (Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23 mybench/build.sh) uses CMake build type RelWithDebInfo with Ninja; compiler not named
corrections.stars_or_usage: 347 stars (1a1a11a/libCacheSim, simulator home of S3FIFO.c); artifact repo Thesys-lab/sosp23-s3fifo 145 stars; CacheLib prototype in Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23
corrections.caveats: The throughput numbers come from a single synthetic Zipf(1.0) workload in a modified CacheLib, not from production traces. The miss-ratio results come from simulation. The paper names no CPU model (only CloudLab c6420 nodes) and no compiler, so this stays at tier B. The S3-FIFO simulator code is in libCacheSim (libCacheSim/cache/eviction/S3FIFO.c). The throughput prototype is in a separate CacheLib fork snapshot (Thesys-lab/cachelib-sosp23, Apache-2.0).

notes: The record's '1559 evaluated traces' does not appear in the paper, which says 6594 traces from 14 datasets. The record also said the throughput test replayed CDN/Twitter/Meta traces, but the paper says it used only a synthetic Zipf trace. Both are fixed. gh metadata matches the record: Apache-2.0, 347 stars, last commit 2026-09-26, active (GitHub lists the repo language as C++, while S3FIFO.c is C).

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed NSDI'21 paper. Its abstract states up to 40% higher single-thread throughput than Memcached and close to 8x at 24 threads (Sec. 4.4.2: >70 MQPS vs 9 MQPS), and Sec. 3.4 states 5 bytes/object metadata, 91% less than Memcached. The CPU is stated (dual Xeon Gold 6230R) and the benchmark code is public (repo benchmarks/, trace_replay_seg), but no compiler or flags are stated, so it is not A.

corrections.workload: Closed-loop trace replay against the storage subsystem only (the networking stack is not exercised), on dedicated Twitter production hosts. It replays week-long unsampled Twitter cache traces (c, u1, u2, n, and a multi-tenant mix) at 1 to 24 threads, measuring MQPS, relative miss ratio, memory footprint and per-object metadata.
corrections.caveats: Memcached 1.6.6 with segmented LRU was tested in two modes (s-Memcached with scanning, and plain Memcached). Throughput was measured on the storage module via trace replay, not end to end over the network. No compiler or flags are stated. The README says this repo is no longer maintained and Segcache was re-implemented in Rust Pelikan. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file is the Apache-2.0 text (Copyright Twitter).

notes: This duplicates the already-verified Pelikan/Segcache entry (same NSDI'21 numbers), so I only did a quick confirm. The numbers and hardware match the paper. gh shows 120 stars, last commit 2023-05-15 (>3 years ago, so abandoned is correct), not archived, not a fork.
